title: At the center of the tuning fork
caption: The lenticular galaxy Mrk 820, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Mrk 820 · constellation Bootes · about 300 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: ESA/Hubble & NASA and N. Grogin (STScI) Acknowledgement: Judy Schmidt (http://www.geckzilla.com/)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Mrk 820 shows hints of spiral structure set inside a round halo of stars. Around it, a scattering of other galaxies covers nearly every type, elliptical and spiral. The bright object at the bottom is not a galaxy but a foreground star called TYC 4386-787-1. Most of the other smears and specks are distant galaxies.

Mrk 820 is a lenticular galaxy, classed as S0 on the Hubble Tuning Fork, a scheme that sorts galaxies by shape. Elliptical galaxies, which look like smooth blobs, sit along the handle, ordered by how stretched they are. The rounder ones sit farthest from the prongs, and the more egg-shaped ones sit near the point where the handle splits.

The two prongs hold the spiral galaxies, one for unbarred spirals and one for barred spirals. Lenticular galaxies like Mrk 820 fall in the transition zone between ellipticals and spirals, right at the fork.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.12 x 1.63 arcminutes) and distance (300 million light years), the frame spans roughly 272,000 × 142,000 light-years. Its light set out about 300 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys observed Mrk 820 through two filters in visible and near-infrared light. The color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: Part of this light is near-infrared, which the eye cannot see, and the galaxy is far too faint for unaided eyes.

explore: Mrk 820 lies about 300 million light-years away. Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys took the picture, and Judy Schmidt entered a version of it in the Hubble's Hidden Treasures image processing competition.
alt: A lenticular galaxy with faint hints of spiral structure in a round halo of stars, surrounded by many small galaxies, with a bright foreground star at the bottom.
